The fiscal 2025 Form 10-K dates three developments in these matters to a specific day or month in calendar 2025. All are in Item 3, Legal Proceedings, and the related risk-factor discussion (AAPL_2025_10K.pdf).

**April 23, 2025 — European Commission actions under the Digital Markets Act.** The Commission fined Apple €500 million in the Article 5(4) investigation and issued a cease-and-desist order requiring Apple to remove technical and commercial restrictions that prevent developers from steering users to distribution channels outside the App Store. Apple has appealed that decision. The same day, the Commission issued preliminary findings in the separate Article 6(4) investigation into Apple’s contractual requirements for third-party app developers and app marketplaces. A final finding of violation could lead to a further cease-and-desist order and fines of up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales.

**April 30, 2025 — Epic Games injunction ruling.** The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California found Apple in violation of the 2021 injunction. It enjoined Apple from imposing any commission or fee on purchases consumers make outside an app; from restricting, conditioning, limiting, or prohibiting how developers guide consumers to those purchases; and from otherwise interfering with a consumer’s choice to proceed in or out of an app. The court denied Apple’s motion to narrow or vacate the injunction and referred Apple to the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California to determine whether criminal contempt proceedings are appropriate. Apple has appealed to the Ninth Circuit. A stay pending appeal was denied.

**September 2, 2025 — remedies in the Google antitrust case.** The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ordered remedies after finding on August 5, 2024, that Google violated U.S. antitrust laws. The order remains subject to further district-court proceedings and to appeals by both the Department of Justice and Google. The filing says a reversal on appeal could result in remedies the DOJ initially proposed, including a prohibition on Google offering Apple commercial terms for search distribution, which could materially reduce Apple’s licensing revenue from those arrangements.

**October 2025 — Epic appeal argument.** The Ninth Circuit agreed to hear Apple’s appeal of the April 30 decision on an expedited basis, and oral arguments were heard in October 2025. The filing does not give a specific day.

Other matters described in the same section, including the March 21, 2024 Department of Justice smartphone monopolization lawsuit and related private antitrust suits, have no calendar-2025 date attached to a development.

Berkshire Hathaway’s 2022 Form 10-K attributes Precision Castparts’ (PCC’s) 11.6% revenue decline in 2021, from 2020 to $6.5 billion, to the COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic caused material declines in commercial air travel and original-equipment-manufacturer (OEM) aircraft production in both 2020 and 2021. PCC’s revenues were reduced in both years by lower aircraft production, which reflected airline order delays and cancellations and industry inventory-reduction initiatives.

More broadly, the filing says the pandemic produced significant adverse effects on PCC’s aerospace business in 2020 and 2021. Sudden, material reductions in air travel led to aircraft build-rate reductions and customer destocking at extraordinary rates. Production delays in Boeing’s 737 MAX and 787 programs over that period also adversely affected PCC.

The filing explains the charges in Management’s Discussion and Analysis, under Other Critical Accounting Policies (pages K-62 to K-63). Related discussion appears in the results of operations and in the “Other” earnings section.

In the second quarter of 2020, Berkshire quantitatively reevaluated goodwill for impairment for certain reporting units, most significantly Precision Castparts (PCC).
